deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page is headed 'Beweis des Reciprocitätsgesetzes unter den Resten und Nichtresten, deren Grad eine Primzahl ist'. That is almost word for word the title of Kummer's 1859 Berlin memoir on the general reciprocity law for λ-th power residues in the cyclotomic field Q(α), with α^λ = 1 and λ an odd prime. The same sheet carries an Italian newspaper dated July 1865, so this page very probably belongs to Riemann's Italian period (1863–65) despite the bundle label '1853'. This page is scratch work toward that proof. It has two parts: (A) bookkeeping rules for a symbol (a_1,…,a_k; b) under products, and (B) a small divisibility computation in Z[α].

(A) Symbol calculus.
Notation (my reading): Π z = z_1 z_2 ⋯ z_{λ-1}. Π^{-1} z_{μ'} is the product with one factor z_μ removed, and Π^{-2} the product with two factors removed. The symbol ( · ; · ) has its first slot or slots separated from the last by a semicolon. The overscripts -2, -3 on y_{ν'} mark the corresponding stage of the iteration; their exact meaning is not certain.

1. First line:
(Π z · y_ν ; y_{ν'}) = Σ_μ Π^{-1} z_{μ'} · y_ν · (z_μ ; y_{ν'}) + Π z · (y_ν ; y_{ν'}).
This is a Leibniz rule in the first slot. The symbol of a product equals the sum, over the factors, of (product of the other factors) × (symbol of that factor). It is the rule δ(ab) = a δb + b δa, iterated. It is therefore additive in this derivation sense, not multiplicative as Hilbert/Legendre-type symbols are.

2. Second and fourth lines:
(Π^{-1} z_{μ'} y_{ν_1} y_{ν_2} ; z_{μ_1} ; y_{ν'}) = Σ_{μ_2} Π^{-2} z_{μ'} y_{ν_1} y_{ν_2} (z_{μ_2}, z_{μ_1} ; y_{ν'}) + Π^{-1} z_{μ'} y_{ν_1} (y_{ν_2}, z_{μ_1} ; y_{ν'}) + Π^{-1} z_{μ'} y_{ν_2} (y_{ν_1}, z_{μ_1} ; y_{ν'}).
This is the same Leibniz rule applied in a further slot of a multi-slot symbol. Line 2 is a first draft with the slot order reversed; line 4 is the corrected version, with the newly differentiated factor placed first.

3. Struck line. A double sum Σ_{μ_1} Σ_{μ_2} was begun and abandoned.

4. Next line: the third step of the iteration,
(Π^{-2} z_{μ'} y_{ν_1} y_{ν_2} y_{ν_3} ; z_{μ_1}, z_{μ_2} ; y_{ν'}^{(-3)}) = Σ_{μ_3} Π^{-3} z_{μ'} y_{ν_1}y_{ν_2}y_{ν_3} (z_{μ_3}, z_{μ_1}, z_{μ_2} ; y_{ν'}) + Π^{-2} z_{μ'} y_{ν_2}y_{ν_3} (y_{ν_1}, z_{μ_1}, z_{μ_2} ; y_{ν'}) + … (left unfinished).

5. Collecting lines (two-slot level):
Πz (y_{ν_1}, y_{ν_2} ; y_{ν'}) + Σ_μ Π^{-1}z_{μ'} y_{ν_1} (z_μ, y_{ν_2} ; y_{ν'}) = (Πz·y_{ν_1}, y_{ν_2} ; y_{ν'}).
The analogous identity holds with the product sitting in the second slot.

6. Three-slot level, begun:
= Πz (y_{ν_1}, y_{ν_2}, y_{ν_3} ; y_{ν'}) + Σ_μ Π^{-1}z_{μ'} [ y_{ν_1}(z_μ, y_{ν_2}, y_{ν_3} ; y_{ν'}) + y_{ν_2}(z_μ, y_{ν_3}, y_{ν_1}, y_{ν'}) … ].

7. General summary formula:
(z_1y_1, z_2y_2, …, z_{λ-1}y_{λ-1}) = z_1⋯z_{λ-1} (y_1,…,y_{λ-1}) + [mixed terms, e.g. (z_1 y_2 ⋯)(y_1, z_2, …)] + … + y_1⋯y_{λ-1} (z_1,…,z_{λ-1}).
Assume the symbol is a derivation in each slot and multilinear, like a Jacobian determinant ∂(f_1,…,f_{λ-1}) or the wedge d f_1 ∧ … ∧ d f_{λ-1}. Then, since d(z_i y_i) = z_i dy_i + y_i dz_i, one gets (my completion)
(z_1y_1,…,z_ny_n) = Σ_{S⊆{1..n}} (Π_{i∈S} z_i Π_{i∉S} y_i) · (w_1,…,w_n),
with w_i = y_i for i∈S and w_i = z_i for i∉S. This sum has 2^n terms. Riemann wrote only the two extreme terms and one garbled representative mixed term.

What it serves. Kummer's proof of the λ-th power reciprocity law evaluates indices of units and numbers mod (1-α) using logarithmic differential quotients d^k log f(e^v)/dv^k at v = 0. Here Riemann appears to set up a multi-argument differential symbol and its product rule. The purpose is to reduce the symbol of a product of numbers to symbols of the individual factors, as is needed when ψ, φ are decomposed into prime factors. The precise definition of the symbol is not on the page.

(B) Divisibility computation (bottom left).
Given: px = m(1-α)^2 and qx = n(1-α). The manuscript appears to read 'm', but this must be n; see the corrections. From these, pn = q m (1-α).
Riemann parametrises the solutions as x = t(1-α)^2, which gives m = pt and n = q(1-α)t.
Check: p·t(1-α)^2 = pt(1-α)^2 gives m = pt. Then q t(1-α)^2 = n(1-α) gives n = q t (1-α). Then p n = p q t(1-α) = q m (1-α). This is consistent.
The computation links to the previous page's representation ψ/φ = (c_0+…+c_{λ-1}α^{λ-1})/(1-α)^2 − Σa/(1-α)^2 + Σaν/(1-α) + an integer. That is, it handles denominators (1-α)^2 and (1-α) when clearing ψ/φ.
errors: Line 2 is a superseded draft: the slot order (z_{μ_1}, z_{μ_2}, y_{ν'}) and the semicolons are inconsistent with line 4, which Riemann rewrote with the new factor placed first.

The general formula for (z_1y_1,…,z_{λ-1}y_{λ-1}) shows only one mixed term, written in garbled form. The full expansion has 2^{λ-1} terms, one for each choice of y_i or z_i in each slot, and the indexing of the representative term (z_1 y_2 ⋯ z_{λ-1})(y_1, z_2 y_3 ⋯) is not correct as written. This is a sketch, not an error of principle.

If the line really reads qx = m(1-α), then together with px = m(1-α)^2 it forces p = q(1-α) and n = m. That is degenerate and inconsistent with the general parametrisation n = q(1-α)t, m = pt. So the intended reading must be qx = n(1-α).
The three-slot expansion lines are left unfinished: trailing '+', and a missing closing parenthesis and semicolon in y_{ν_2}(z_μ, y_{ν_3}, y_{ν_1}, y_{ν'}.

results.what: Leibniz/product rule for a multi-slot symbol (a_1,…,a_k; b): the symbol of a product equals the sum over factors of (product of the other factors) × (symbol of that factor), iterated slot by slot.
results.modern_name: Product rule for derivations / multilinear expansion of a Jacobian determinant (wedge product of differentials)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard calculus (Leibniz); its use for reciprocity via differential quotients goes back to Kummer (1858–59)

results.what: Full expansion (z_1y_1,…,z_ny_n) = Σ_S Π_{S}z Π_{S^c}y · (mixed arguments), with extreme terms z_1⋯z_n(y_1,…,y_n) and y_1⋯y_n(z_1,…,z_n).
results.modern_name: Multilinearity of the Jacobian / exterior algebra expansion of d(z_1y_1)∧…∧d(z_ny_n)

results.what: Solution of px = m(1-α)^2, qx = n(1-α) in Z[α] by x = t(1-α)^2, m = pt, n = q(1-α)t, consistent with pn = qm(1-α).
results.modern_name: Elementary divisibility by powers of the prime (1-α) above λ in the cyclotomic integers

results.what: Evidence that Riemann worked through Kummer's 1859 proof of the general λ-th power reciprocity law, probably c. 1865 in Italy.
results.modern_name: Kummer's reciprocity law for regular primes (precursor of Hilbert/Artin–Hasse explicit reciprocity)

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra is routine: a product rule for a derivation-type symbol and simple divisibility by powers of (1-α). The mildly interesting point is historical. Together with the previous page, it shows Riemann reworking Kummer's 1859 proof of the general reciprocity law, probably c. 1865. That engagement with Kummer's cyclotomic arithmetic is not widely documented, but nothing here goes beyond Kummer.

The page header '$\Pi z_2$[?]' is uncertain in the image; it is likely an abandoned heading such as 'Πz', and the struck line beneath is 'z_1 z_2 ⋯ z_{λ-1} y_ν'.

First line: the image shows '(Πz y_ν ; y_{ν'}) = Σ_μ Π z_{μ'} y_ν (z_μ, y_{ν'}) + Πz (y)'; the Π on the right carries an overscript -1 elsewhere, and the final term is a truncated '(y_ν ; y_{ν'})', as in the rewritten third line.

In the mixed term of the general formula, '(z_1 y_2 ⋯ z_{λ-1})(y_1, z_2 y_3 ⋯ z_{λ-1})' is garbled in the image. It is a representative mixed term with a coefficient product and argument list in which y_i and z_i are swapped relative to the coefficient.
